unit.title: The Sikh Diaspora's Institutions and Impact

lesson.title: Review Day: The Sikh Diaspora's Institutions and Impact
lesson.subject: sikhi

contentBlocks.text: This week you went deeper into the diaspora's institutions and real-world impact. Let's review it all!

Quick review: the diaspora is concentrated in several distinct world regions today (Day 1). Diaspora Gurdwaras expanded into genuine civic centers (Day 2). Diaspora organizations are well-known for Langar-based humanitarian relief work (Day 3). The diaspora actively works to preserve language and culture across generations (Day 4). Write a short paragraph explaining how these four themes together show the diaspora as an active, living community, not just people who moved somewhere new and stayed the same.

Great work this week — you explored the diaspora's real institutions and impact in genuine depth! A future unit will explore the historical drivers of colonialism and the 1947 partition behind much of this migration, with the depth and care they deserve.

objectives: Review diaspora regions, expanded Gurdwara civic role, humanitarian contributions, and language preservation
Write a short paragraph connecting all four themes into one picture of an active, living diaspora
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child write their connecting paragraph.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of diaspora institutions and impact, and note that a future unit will explore colonialism and partition with the depth they deserve.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just two of the four themes the child remembers best rather than requiring all four in the paragraph
Ready for more: ask the child which of the four themes they find most personally meaningful, and why
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four diaspora-impact themes needs the most reinforcement going forward, and re-affirms the deliberate deferral of colonialism/partition content
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended synthesis activity — check that the paragraph connects at least two or three of the week's themes into a coherent picture, for example noting that the diaspora's institutions (Gurdwaras), values in action (humanitarian relief), and ongoing effort (language preservation) together show a community actively building and sustaining its identity, not simply existing passively in a new place.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's global-diaspora thread before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session, and explicitly re-affirms the deliberate deferral of colonialism and the 1947 partition to a future, dedicated unit.
